chunks: Muhammad ibn Adam from al-Rida (peace be upon him) in [the matter of]

When a man says to his slave girl, 'I have freed you, and I have made your dowry your freedom,' he said: 'The manumission is valid and the choice is hers; if she wishes, she may marry herself [to him], and if she wishes, she may not. If she marries herself, then I would like for him to give her something, so that it does not contradict the earlier reports, because the choice is hers only if he begins the statement with manumission before marriage. For the manumission proceeds, and she is left with the choice regarding the marriage contract. And it is proper that he begin with marriage and make the dowry the manumission, so that the contract is valid and the marriage proceeds, and that which indicates this distinction is...'
ai.seo_question: What is the proper legal procedure when a master frees his slave girl and makes her freedom her dowry?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Rida (AS) to resolve the apparent contradiction between earlier narrations regarding the sequence of manumission and marriage. The Imam clarifies that if manumission precedes the marriage proposal, the woman holds the exclusive right of choice (*khayr*) in accepting the contract, whereas initiating with marriage ensures immediate validity. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the woman's agency in marital contracts when her status transitions from slave to free.
